messages.author: 65f44d9fbdf788d4
messages.subject: Corrplot not working all of a sudden
parts:
Hi D-Rug community,
I recently updated R and now my corrplot() code that was working before throws an error when I try and use it. Specifically, it won't work when I ask it to plot only significant variables. 

Here is the old code I had: 
corrplot(res3$r, order="hclust", 
         p.mat = res3$P, sig.level = 0.05, insig = "blank",tl.cex=1.5)

I get the error that there are unused arguments (all arguments after res3$r are unused...?). If anyone can shed some light onto how to get this fixed that would be great!

Thanks,
Hannah

--
Hannah Waterhouse, M.S.
PhD Candidate, Soils and Biogeochemistry Graduate Group
University of California, Davis

messages.author: 91fcdff1323a6831
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Corrplot not working all of a sudden
parts:
Hi Hannah,
One additional thought in case the previous options don't work. There may be another corrplot function masked by a different package you have installed. Explicitly calling the corrplot function from the corrplot package may help, in case there's a conflict somewhere. This is similar to a few of the dplyr functions (filter/select/summarize) that conflict with other modeling functions of the same name. To explicitly call a function from a package, we use the following:
  • NameOfPackage::name_of_function()
So, try using:
 corrplot::corrplot(res3$r, order="hclust",
p.mat = res3$P, sig.level = 0.05, insig = "blank",tl.cex=1.5)

And let us know if you get a similar error.

Good luck,
Ryan

Hi, Hannah.  I'm glad this had a happy ending for you, but I'm puzzled by your report: I can't find any "base function corrplot".  See the appended for the evidence.

I took R's helpful suggestion to type:

    ??corrplot

and that did turn up:

    psych::cor.plot

but no additional references to "corrplot".

My concern is just that you might have problems lurking further down the road if you're finding multiple versions of corrplot.  If you're satisfied with the outcome, I promise not to pester you any further.

-- Mike

On Fri, Mar 1, 2019 at 5:25 PM Hannah Waterhouse <hwate...@ucdavis.edu> wrote:
Hey Michael,
Sorry by base corrplot I meant if I just use the basic function on a matrix, corrplot(res3$r) without any other specifications (order="hclust", 
         p.mat = res3$P, sig.level = 0.05, insig = "blank",tl.cex=1.5) it works. But when I added these specifications in it didn't work unless I used Ryan's suggestion and used:

corrplot::corrplot(res3$r, order="hclust", 
         p.mat = res3$P, sig.level = 0.05, insig = "blank",tl.cex=1.5)

Once I used Ryan's suggestion it worked... 

Prior to this, I tried updating all my packages and that didn't work...

Thank you for the concern! Let me know your thoughts,
Hannah

On Fri, Mar 1, 2019 at 5:09 PM Michael Hannon <jmhannon...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi, Hannah.  I'm glad this had a happy ending for you, but I'm puzzled by your report: I can't find any "base function corrplot".  See the appended for the evidence.

I took R's helpful suggestion to type:

    ??corrplot

and that did turn up:

    psych::cor.plot

but no additional references to "corrplot".

My concern is just that you might have problems lurking further down the road if you're finding multiple versions of corrplot.  If you're satisfied with the outcome, I promise not to pester you any further.

-- Mike
